title: Integration tests split by what they prove: api/ through the request path, persistence/ at the database
context: Route-entry tests proved request mapping and round trips; repository-entry tests proved MongoDB semantics such as arrayFilters and $pull, or how stored documents read back. Several route tests asserted only a schema rejection that happens before the database is reached.
decision: test/integration/api/ holds tests whose assertions depend on a real database read or write reached through a route; they arrange and read data only through routes and repository interfaces, never through the driver. test/integration/persistence/ holds tests of database behaviour itself, entering at a repository or use case, and may use the driver directly. A route test whose assertion does not depend on the database is a route unit test instead. Request validation completes before any use case runs, so a unit test showing the next layer was not called also shows nothing was written.

alternatives.reason: A database change would force a rewrite of every integration test instead of persistence/ alone.

alternatives.option: Route and repository access only, everywhere
alternatives.reason: Whether a field really left the stored document could not be proven.

consequences: A database change concentrates its test rewrite in persistence/, alongside the repository implementations.
revisitTriggers: Acceptance tests that enter at the use case are adopted: a third directory may be needed.
